project.name: alpnav
project.description: AlpNav is a Next.js alpine navigation app that mirrors Zillertal Arena panorama artwork into the repository for fast local delivery. The app uses local static panorama tiles and manifests to support the MVP map experience without runtime dependency on the reference site.

nodes.name: mobile_audit.py
nodes.summary: Runs a regex-driven mobile UX audit over React Native and Flutter files, collecting issues and warnings across touch, performance, navigation, typography, color, platform, backend, and testing heuristics.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a single stateful auditor class with filesystem walking and extensive regex heuristics instead of AST parsing.

nodes.name: MobileAuditor
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the audit state and applies the full suite of mobile design checks to individual files or directories before producing a report.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments, runs the mobile auditor against a file or directory, and prints either JSON or a readable audit report before exiting with a compliance-based status code.

nodes.name: next.config.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Next.js runtime configuration and adds immutable cache headers for resort panorama asset routes so locally mirrored tiles can be served efficiently.

nodes.name: layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the App Router root layout, wires in Google font variables, and exports the global metadata used by the AlpNav shell.

nodes.name: RootLayout
nodes.summary: Wraps every route in the root HTML and body structure while applying the configured font CSS variables to the page body.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Provides the `/` route entry and hands the local Zillertal Arena panorama manifest to the map shell so the homepage can boot directly into the resort view.

nodes.name: Home
nodes.summary: Renders the map shell with the bundled panorama manifest for the homepage experience.

nodes.name: Drawer.tsx
nodes.summary: Slide-out side drawer with menu metadata and focus-trapping behavior for the map shell.

nodes.name: Drawer
nodes.summary: Builds the full slide-out menu panel and coordinates its open state, backdrop, close affordances, and accessible focus behavior.

nodes.name: handleKeyDown
nodes.summary: Handles Escape to close the drawer and traps Tab navigation within the panel so keyboard focus stays inside the dialog while it is open.

nodes.name: hitTest.ts
nodes.summary: Overlay hit-testing utility that prioritizes point markers and then falls back to line-distance matching for lifts and pistes.

nodes.name: minDistToSegments
nodes.summary: Scans polyline segment lists and returns the minimum point-to-segment distance used by overlay selection logic.

nodes.name: hitTestOverlays
nodes.summary: Priority-ordered hit-test across overlay entities.

nodes.name: ImageCarousel.tsx
nodes.summary: Touch-friendly image carousel used inside the info sheet for looping resort media galleries.

nodes.name: ImageCarousel
nodes.summary: Looping image carousel component used by the info sheet.

nodes.name: handleTransitionEnd
nodes.summary: Resets the strip position after animating onto a cloned slide so the carousel can loop seamlessly without a visible jump.

nodes.name: handleTouchMove
nodes.summary: Locks gesture direction and updates the horizontal drag offset only when the interaction is identified as a horizontal swipe.

nodes.name: handleTouchEnd
nodes.summary: Finishes a swipe gesture, decides whether to advance the carousel, and clears transient drag state.

nodes.name: InfoSheet.tsx
nodes.summary: Bottom sheet UI for the selected map item. It switches between piste, lift, gastronomy, webcam, infrastructure, and sport-fun variants, manages swipe-to-dismiss and lightbox state, and delegates image browsing to the carousel.

nodes.name: MapShell.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side map shell that boots Pixi and pixi-viewport, streams panorama tile levels, draws all overlay layers, wires hit testing and selection state, and renders the surrounding control chrome.

nodes.name: drawGastronomyMarkerOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Pixi marker renderer for gastronomy POIs that paints colored circular badges first and then overlays a fork-and-knife glyph for each spot.

nodes.name: drawHighlightOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Selection highlight helpers for the map. It redraws pistes, lifts, and marker badges in a gold accent so the currently selected item stays visible above the base overlays.

nodes.name: drawInfrastructureOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Pixi marker renderer for infrastructure POIs using color-coded rounded badges and category-specific symbols for parking, bus, info, and rescue points.

nodes.name: drawLabelOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Tiered label renderer that groups parsed map labels into four Pixi containers so callers can reveal richer annotation layers as zoom increases.

nodes.name: drawLiftMarkerOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Pixi marker renderer for lift icons. It paints the shared green lift badge and then draws a lift-type glyph for gondola, chairlift, or drag-lift markers.

nodes.name: drawLiftOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Draws lift linework and terminal circles into a Pixi container using the normalized lift geometry from the resort overlay dataset.

nodes.name: drawPisteMarkerOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Renders piste number badges, difficulty colors, and closed-slope slashes for slope icon locations in the map scene.

nodes.name: drawPisteOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Paints piste polylines grouped by difficulty and converts ski-route segments into dashed Pixi strokes.

nodes.name: drawSportFunOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Builds hexagonal sport-fun badges and category-specific glyphs for interactive activity points on the map.

nodes.name: drawWebcamMarkerOverlay.ts
nodes.summary: Draws webcam badges and a simplified camera glyph for webcam POIs in the panorama map overlay.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the local panorama manifest schema that describes tile dimensions and zoom-level metadata for mirrored resort panoramas.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses exported object type aliases instead of interfaces to keep manifest shapes lightweight and colocated with the map feature.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the shared AlpNav domain model for pistes, lifts, labels, POIs, webcams, and the aggregate overlay payload consumed across the map feature.
nodes.languageNotes: This file uses object and union type aliases to model normalized resort data without introducing runtime code.

nodes.name: adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Loads mirrored Zillertal Arena overlay assets, translates metadata into English, and adapts SVG and JSON sources into the normalized ResortOverlayData structure.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines DOM-based SVG parsing with TypeScript domain types to normalize static resort assets into a typed overlay payload.

nodes.name: InfoSheet
nodes.summary: Main selection sheet component that adapts its layout to the currently selected overlay entity and coordinates drag dismissal, live webcam mode, and image lightbox behavior.

nodes.name: pisteSubtitle
nodes.summary: Builds the subtitle shown for a piste by combining difficulty text with length when available.

nodes.name: liftSubtitle
nodes.summary: Builds the subtitle shown for a lift from its type, capacity, and altitude delta metadata.

nodes.name: LiftTypeIcon
nodes.summary: Inline SVG badge component that renders lift-specific iconography matching the map markers.

nodes.name: MapShell
nodes.summary: Primary interactive map component that initializes rendering, loads overlay data, attaches viewport behaviors, and owns selection, debug, drawer, and filter state.

nodes.name: MapControlButton
nodes.summary: Shared bottom-bar toggle button used for the major overlay controls.

nodes.name: DifficultyFilterPanel
nodes.summary: Popover control for toggling piste difficulty filters and the aggregate all-on state.

nodes.name: LegendPanel
nodes.summary: Legend popover that explains slope, lift, and gastronomy visual encodings.

nodes.name: loadLevelIntoViewport
nodes.summary: Loads a panorama zoom level into Pixi by fetching tile textures, cropping edge tiles, and attaching the resulting sprites to a level container.

nodes.name: createTileDescriptors
nodes.summary: Derives world-space tile descriptors for one panorama level from the manifest and current max zoom level.

nodes.name: applyLevelBlend
nodes.summary: Controls which loaded panorama levels are visible and how much the upper level fades in as zoom approaches the next threshold.

nodes.name: computeMinScale
nodes.summary: Computes the minimum allowed viewport scale so the panorama fits inside the current screen with a small margin.

nodes.name: buildTileUrl
nodes.summary: Builds the local panorama tile URL for a given remote zoom and tile coordinate.

nodes.name: drawGastronomyMarkerOverlay
nodes.summary: Draws gastronomy badges in two passes so the circular fills and the white utensil icons stay separate.

nodes.name: drawPisteHighlight
nodes.summary: Renders the selected piste with an outer difficulty-colored stroke and an inner gold stroke, including dashed ski routes.

nodes.name: drawLiftHighlight
nodes.summary: Redraws the selected lift's line and terminals in gold while preserving the original overlay geometry.

nodes.name: drawBadgeHighlight
nodes.summary: Applies the gold selection outline for badge-based entities such as webcams, gastronomy, infrastructure, sport-fun, pistes, and lifts.

nodes.name: drawDashedSegment
nodes.summary: Helper that converts a polyline into alternating dash and gap draw commands for ski-route highlights.

nodes.name: drawInfrastructureOverlay
nodes.summary: Draws infrastructure POI badges and their category glyphs as separate Pixi passes.

nodes.name: drawLabelOverlay
nodes.summary: Builds four label containers, paints optional background rectangles, and adds Pixi Text nodes for each tier.

nodes.name: drawLiftMarkerOverlay
nodes.summary: Draws lift icon markers in two passes using a shared badge fill and a glyph chosen from the lift type.

nodes.name: drawGondola
nodes.summary: Renders the gondola marker glyph with cable, clamp, hangers, cabin deck, and windows.

nodes.name: drawChairlift
nodes.summary: Renders the chairlift marker glyph with cable, hanger bracket, seat, and footrest.

nodes.name: drawDragLift
nodes.summary: Renders the drag-lift marker glyph with cable, hanger pole, and T-bar.

nodes.name: loadArenaOverlayData
nodes.summary: Memoizes loading of the Arena overlay payload so callers share one parsing promise for the mirrored static assets.

nodes.name: drawPisteOverlay
nodes.summary: Groups pistes by difficulty for solid strokes and renders ski-route segments with dashed linework in separate Pixi graphics objects.

nodes.name: drawLiftOverlay
nodes.summary: Builds lift outlines, inner strokes, and terminal markers for every lift segment before attaching the graphics to the scene container.

nodes.name: drawPisteMarkerOverlay
nodes.summary: Renders piste-number badges with difficulty-specific fills and overlays text labels for each piste icon position.

nodes.name: drawWebcamMarkerOverlay
nodes.summary: Paints rounded webcam badges and reuses a camera-icon helper to mark webcam positions on the map.

nodes.name: drawSportFunOverlay
nodes.summary: Creates colored hex badges for sport-fun POIs and delegates glyph drawing for each category to the shared icon helper.

nodes.name: drawDashedSegment
nodes.summary: Converts a piste polyline into alternating dash and gap segments so ski routes can be rendered with dashed strokes.

nodes.name: drawIcon
nodes.summary: Draws category-specific white glyphs for skimovie, speed check, depot, photo point, and viewpoint badges.

nodes.name: fetchAndParse
nodes.summary: Fetches mirrored SVG and JSON overlay assets, parses them into DOM documents, and assembles the final normalized overlay payload.

nodes.name: buildPisteMetaMap
nodes.summary: Extracts piste names, difficulty, numbering, length, and status from the raw arena JSON into a lookup map keyed by overlay feature id.

nodes.name: translateInfrastructureTitle
nodes.summary: Translates infrastructure titles from German naming conventions into English UI labels.

nodes.name: translateInfrastructureDescription
nodes.summary: Normalizes selected German infrastructure description fragments into English text for the UI.

nodes.name: translateLiftDescription
nodes.summary: Applies a sequence of German-to-English replacements and numeric normalization rules to lift descriptions.

nodes.name: buildLiftMetaMap
nodes.summary: Builds a metadata lookup for lifts, including type normalization, elevations, images, translated descriptions, and opening hours.

nodes.name: parseGastronomy
nodes.summary: Transforms gastronomy POIs from raw arena JSON into normalized map spots with translated coordinates and media metadata.

nodes.name: parseInfrastructure
nodes.summary: Maps infrastructure category buckets into normalized POI records with translated titles, descriptions, status, and images.

nodes.name: parseSportFun
nodes.summary: Converts sport-fun POI groups into normalized activity points with translated titles, status, and media metadata.

nodes.name: parseWebcams
nodes.summary: Combines feratel and panomax webcam buckets into a shared webcam model with provider detection and normalized positions.

nodes.name: normalizeDifficulty
nodes.summary: Maps raw piste difficulty strings to the constrained PisteDifficulty union used across the app.

nodes.name: normalizeLiftType
nodes.summary: Converts numeric lift type identifiers from the source data into the app’s LiftType union.

nodes.name: parsePistes
nodes.summary: Walks piste SVG groups, parses path geometry and icon circles, and merges metadata into normalized piste records.

nodes.name: parseLifts
nodes.summary: Extracts lift polylines and icon positions from the lift SVG and enriches them with lift metadata before returning normalized lift records.

nodes.name: parseLabels
nodes.summary: Parses text and polygon background elements from the text SVG to produce tiered map labels with optional badge geometry.

nodes.name: parsePolylinePoints
nodes.summary: Converts SVG polyline coordinate strings into scaled world-space point arrays.

nodes.name: parseSvgPathD
nodes.summary: Tokenizes and approximates SVG path commands into scaled polyline segments suitable for Pixi rendering.

nodes.name: sampleCubic
nodes.summary: Samples cubic Bezier segments into intermediate points so curved SVG paths can be rendered as polylines.

nodes.name: PanoramaLevel
nodes.summary: Defines one mirrored panorama zoom level, including dimensions, grid size, and its mapping back to the source zoom level.

nodes.name: PanoramaManifest
nodes.summary: Describes the full mirrored panorama tile manifest for a resort, including URL template and available zoom levels.

nodes.name: Point
nodes.summary: Represents a 2D world-space coordinate shared by all parsed overlay geometry.

nodes.name: Piste
nodes.summary: Defines the normalized piste model, combining geometry, metadata, numbering, icons, and optional ski-route segments.

nodes.name: Lift
nodes.summary: Defines the normalized lift model with path geometry, icon placement, operating details, and optional media metadata.

nodes.name: MapLabel
nodes.summary: Models parsed map label text, styling, tiering, and optional badge background geometry from the text overlay SVG.

nodes.name: GastronomySpot
nodes.summary: Defines a normalized gastronomy POI with category, position, description, imagery, and optional website data.

nodes.name: InfrastructurePoi
nodes.summary: Defines a normalized infrastructure POI for parking, buses, information, and rescue points.

nodes.name: SportFunPoi
nodes.summary: Defines a normalized sport-fun POI with a dedicated sportCategory discriminant to avoid overlap with infrastructure data.

nodes.name: Webcam
nodes.summary: Defines the webcam POI model with provider, position, thumbnail, and streaming URL fields.

nodes.name: ResortOverlayData
nodes.summary: Aggregates every parsed overlay collection into the typed payload consumed by the map feature.

layers.name: Tooling Layer
layers.description: Project-local analysis tooling that supports development workflows outside the AlpNav runtime.

layers.name: Config Layer
layers.description: Next.js runtime and shell configuration that sets up AlpNav metadata, fonts, and asset caching behavior.

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: Route and client-facing React components that present the panorama experience and map controls to the user.

layers.name: Map Rendering Layer
layers.description: Feature-support modules that perform overlay hit testing and draw the Pixi-based resort graphics consumed by the map shell.

layers.name: Types Layer
layers.description: Static panorama contracts and normalized domain models shared across AlpNav's map UI, rendering, and data-loading paths.

layers.name: Data Service Layer
layers.description: Static resort-data adaptation logic that translates mirrored Zillertal Arena assets into the normalized overlay payload used by the app.

tour.title: Homepage Entry
tour.description: Start at `src/app/page.tsx`, the `/` route that boots the MVP immediately into the local panorama experience. This file is intentionally thin: it proves the homepage is data-backed by mirrored assets and passes control straight into the large map feature rather than spreading boot logic across the route layer.

tour.title: Map Shell Orchestrator
tour.description: From the route entry, move into `src/features/map/MapShell.tsx`, which is the real center of gravity for the product. It boots Pixi and the viewport, loads panorama levels, requests normalized resort overlays, and coordinates the chrome around the canvas, so understanding this file gives a newcomer the full homepage boot path in one place.

tour.title: Panorama Manifest Contract
tour.description: Next, inspect `src/features/map/types.ts`, which defines the local panorama manifest schema consumed at boot. This contract explains how mirrored tile metadata is represented in-repo, and it clarifies why AlpNav can deliver the initial map view without calling the reference site at runtime.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript object type aliases work well for data-only contracts like manifests because they stay lightweight while still giving strong editor help and compile-time validation.

tour.title: Shared Domain Model
tour.description: Once the panorama contract is clear, read `src/lib/domain/types.ts` to learn the vocabulary used everywhere else: pistes, lifts, labels, POIs, webcams, and the aggregate overlay payload. This file has the highest fan-in in the graph, which makes it the best anchor for understanding how the UI, adapter, hit testing, and renderers all agree on the same normalized resort shapes.
tour.languageLesson: This file leans on exported unions and object types to model a rich domain without adding runtime code, a common TypeScript pattern when many subsystems need to share the same normalized shapes.

tour.title: Arena Data Adapter
tour.description: With the domain model in mind, move to `src/lib/resorts/arena/adapter.ts`, which translates mirrored Zillertal Arena SVG and JSON assets into `ResortOverlayData`. This is the bridge between static local source material and the typed structures consumed by the map shell, so it explains how AlpNav mirrors the reference artwork while staying runtime-independent.

tour.title: Selection Flow
tour.description: After the adapter feeds the shell, study the user interaction loop across `src/features/map/hitTest.ts`, `src/features/map/InfoSheet.tsx`, and `src/features/map/Drawer.tsx`. These files show how pointer input turns into selected domain entities, how details are surfaced to the user, and how surrounding controls support the map without competing with the canvas-driven experience.

tour.title: Overlay Rendering Core
tour.description: Now treat the overlay rendering subsystem as one feature area, starting with the shared linework and annotation renderers. `drawLiftOverlay`, `drawPisteOverlay`, `drawLabelOverlay`, and `drawHighlightOverlay` show how normalized resort data becomes visible map structure, readable labels, and selection feedback layered on top of the panorama scene.

tour.title: Overlay Marker Family
tour.description: Finish with the marker-focused overlay files, which round out the feature by rendering the interactive POIs visitors actually tap on. `drawLiftMarkerOverlay`, `drawGastronomyMarkerOverlay`, `drawInfrastructureOverlay`, `drawSportFunOverlay`, and `drawWebcamMarkerOverlay` reuse the same domain payload but specialize the visual language for each resort entity category, giving a new engineer a clean map of where to extend overlay coverage next.
